test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 2 children:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.
  - Blake is 20 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

Regarding Blake:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 20, which is 20 or over
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to know a bit about your child (or children). 

**First, can you tell me:**
1. **How old is your child?** (Or if you have multiple children, let's start with one and we'll go through each)
2. **What is your child's name?** (This helps me keep track if you have multiple children)

The age is important because:
- Children **under 16** automatically qualify (subject to other conditions)
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **20 or over** generally don't qualify

Please share these details and we'll work through your eligibility together.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have two children actually. 

My youngest is Alex, who's 8 years old. 

And then I have Blake, who's 20.

Should we start with Alex?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Yes, let's start with Alex, and then we'll assess Blake separately.

**For Alex (8 years old):**

Since Alex is under 16, that's a good start. Now I need to check a few more things.

**Is Alex working full-time?** (This would mean working 24 hours or more per week in paid employment)

This is very rare for an 8-year-old, but I need to ask as it's part of the official criteria.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, not at all. Alex is only 8, so no work at all - just school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Let me continue with Alex's assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now, the next question:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in their own right?** (Such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)

Again, this would be unusual for an 8-year-old, but I need to check all the criteria.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't get any benefits in their own name. Nothing like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Next question:

**Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

(Again, very unlikely for an 8-year-old, but this is part of the official checklist!)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not. Alex is just in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let's move on to questions about **you** as the claimant.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status:

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

This means the UK is your main home where you usually reside. If you do, that satisfies the residency requirement.

(There are also other ways to qualify if you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or if you're a Crown servant abroad, but let's start with the most common situation.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Living in Manchester definitely meets the residency requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now about your responsibility for Alex:

**Do you live with Alex?** 

(Or if not living together, do you contribute to Alex's upkeep by paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their care?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now an important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** 

For example, Alex's other parent or another family member? 

(Only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child at a time.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Which of these applies to Alex:**
- Living normally at home with you (most common)
- Currently in hospital
- In local authority care
- In a fostering arrangement

What's Alex's situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is just living normally at home with me. Nothing special like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue checking.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! One final question about Alex:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

(This would mean the council is contributing financially to Alex's housing or care costs.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me check the outcome for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news for Alex!** Based on the assessment, you **are eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex (8 years old). ✓

Now, let's assess **Blake (20 years old)**. Let me start their assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**For Blake (20 years old):**

Unfortunately, I need to inform you that according to the Child Benefit rules, **children aged 20 or over are not eligible** for Child Benefit, regardless of their circumstances (education, employment, etc.).

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Let me now provide you with the complete assessment for both children:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
---

## **Summary of Your Child Benefit Eligibility**

### **For Alex (8 years old): ✅ ELIGIBLE**
You meet all the requirements for Child Benefit for Alex. 

**Next steps for Alex:**
- **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
- Provide **proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
- Provide Alex's **birth certificate** or adoption certificate
- **Important:** Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year (you may need to pay some or all of it back through tax)
- Payments are made **every 4 weeks** (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

**Apply here:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

---

### **For Blake (20 years old): ❌ NOT ELIGIBLE**
Unfortunately, Blake does not qualify because they are 20 years old. Child Benefit stops at age 20, even if the young person is in education or training. The benefit can continue until age 19 for those in approved education/training, but once they turn 20, eligibility ends.

**Additional information:** If Blake turned 20 recently and you were previously receiving Child Benefit for them, those payments would have stopped on their 20th birthday (or at the end of the benefit week containing their birthday).

---

If you have any questions about applying for Alex or need clarification on anything, please let me know!

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old (under 16), not working full-time, not receiving benefits in their own right, not in an apprenticeship, lives with you in the UK (Manchester), you meet UK residency requirements, no one else is claiming for Alex, Alex is living normally at home (not in hospital/care), and the local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. Alex meets all the Child Benefit eligibility criteria.

Blake is 20 years old. According to Child Benefit rules, children aged 20 or over do not qualify for Child Benefit regardless of their education status, employment situation, or any other circumstances. The maximum age limit for Child Benefit is 19 (for those in approved education or training), and this stops when the young person turns 20.

The claimant is eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, who meets all requirements as a child under 16 living at home. However, Blake is ineligible because they are 20 years old, which exceeds the maximum age limit for Child Benefit (19 years for those in education/training).
